headline: Local Dairyman Confused After Canadian Tariff Announcement Forces Him To Accept Payment In Politely-Worded Apologies
body:
For Ranjit Singh, a dairy farmer in Karnal who exports select artisanal ghee to a single boutique shop in Ottawa, the recent news of punitive tariffs on dairy goods has taken a surreal turn. Instead of adjusting his invoices or navigating complex tax codes, Singh was notified via email that his future shipments would now be compensated strictly in the form of 'sincere, multi-paragraph written apologies' from government bureaucrats.

'I don’t know what to do with these,' Singh said, brandishing a printed-out letter from a trade official that expressed profound regret over the rising cost of imported yogurt. 'I tried to take it to the local bank to pay for my feed supplies, but the manager told me the exchange rate for a 'deeply felt sorrow' clause is currently lower than the value of scrap paper.'

Trade analysts suggest this unorthodox payment method is part of a broader, yet highly specific, regional initiative to ensure trade disputes remain excessively courteous. While the dairy sector scrambles to understand the liquidity of an official written lamentation, Canadian customs officials have reportedly promised that if the ghee arrives even slightly chilled, the apologies will be upgraded to 'hand-written notes with a maple-leaf watermark.'

Singh remains optimistic but weary, noting that his suppliers are increasingly unwilling to accept a letter of 'collective moral hesitation' as legal tender for tractor fuel. 'They told me that unless the apology mentions my family by name and includes a suggestion for a nice weekend hike, it’s not worth the ink it’s printed with,' he added.
caption: When the trade war hits the local supply chain, even the butter starts apologizing. Is a heartfelt letter of regret enough to cover your overheads? #TradeTalks #CanadaDairy #GlobalEconomics #Satire (satire)
